title: Continuous differentials of a formal power-series ring
statement: Let $F$ be a field, $n\ge0$, $D=F[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], and $\mathfrak n=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$. Define $\widehat\Omega_{D/F}=\varprojlim_r\Omega_{(D/\mathfrak n^r)/F}$ using the quotient transition maps and let $\widehat{\mathrm d}:D\to\widehat\Omega_{D/F}$ send $h$ to the compatible family of its Kähler differentials. Then $\widehat\Omega_{D/F}$ is a free $D$-module with basis $\widehat{\mathrm d}(t_1),\ldots,\widehat{\mathrm d}(t_n)$; equivalently, the map $D^{\oplus n}\to\widehat\Omega_{D/F}$ sending the $i$-th basis vector to $\widehat{\mathrm d}(t_i)$ is an isomorphism. For every $h\in D$, $\widehat{\mathrm d}(h)=\sum_i(\partial h/\partial t_i)\widehat{\mathrm d}(t_i)$, where the partial derivatives are the termwise formal derivatives [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative].

source.place: Tag 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring, lines 34310-34340), polynomial basis and derivative formula, and Tag 02HQ (lemma-differential-mod-power-ideal, lines 34194-34209), comparison modulo powers. This auxiliary continuous inverse-limit statement is not stated in Curves Tag 0C4D; the truncation/completion argument remains to be split in this unsplit node.

proof.text: Use positive levels as in [def-trf-continuous-kahler-differentials]; an exponent-zero term is $\Omega_{0/F}=0$ and adds no condition. Put $P=F[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, $J=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\subset P$, $M=D^{\oplus n}$ and $Q_r=D/\mathfrak n^r$. By [lem-trf-power-series-truncated-differential-presentation], the coordinate maps $\theta_r:M\to\Omega_{Q_r/F}$ are surjective and $K_r=\ker\theta_r$ is $\mathfrak n^rM$ plus the span of polynomial gradients from $J^r$. By [lem-trf-power-series-adic-gradient-control], these gradients lie in $\mathfrak n^{r-1}M$. Hence $\mathfrak n^rM\subseteq K_r\subseteq\mathfrak n^{r-1}M$.

The quotient differential transition $\rho_r$ sends $\mathrm d(b)$ to $\mathrm d(\bar b)$ [def-trf-continuous-kahler-differentials]. Thus $\rho_r\theta_{r+1}(a)=\sum_i(a_i\bmod\mathfrak n^r)\mathrm d(t_i\bmod\mathfrak n^r)=\theta_r(a)$; iterate for all levels. In [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-stable-ranges] take $A=D$, $H=M$, $I=\mathfrak n$, $N_k=\Omega_{Q_{k+1}/F}$, $\rho_k^{\mathrm{there}}=\theta_{k+1}:M\to N_k$, and $\theta_k^{\mathrm{there}}$ its factor through $M/\mathfrak n^{k+1}M$. Step 1 gives this factorization. Compatibility descends to the quotient maps by the displayed identity. With $c=1$ its kernel condition is $K_{k+2}\subseteq\mathfrak n^{k+1}M$. Both $\rho_k^{\mathrm{there}}$ and $N_{k+1}\to N_k$ are surjective, the latter by compatibility and surjectivity of $\theta_{k+2}$. Thus its range condition holds, giving $M^\wedge\cong L=\varprojlim_r\Omega_{Q_r/F}$ with the stated coordinate projections.

source.place: Tag 02OC (theorem-formal-functions), cofinal-kernel inverse-limit argument, via the existing closed stable-ranges lemma with shift one.

proof.text: Coordinatewise reduction $M\to(D/\mathfrak n^r)^{\oplus n}$ is surjective and has kernel $\mathfrak n^rM$: lift each of the finitely many coordinates, and write a vector in the kernel as the sum of its coordinate vectors. Thus $M/\mathfrak n^rM=(D/\mathfrak n^r)^{\oplus n}$ compatibly with reduction. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-variables-complete] and [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], a compatible family has a unique lift in each coordinate. These lifts respect addition and $D$-scalars by uniqueness, so the canonical map $M\to M^\wedge$ to the $\mathfrak n$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] is a $D$-linear isomorphism. Composing with Step 2 gives $\Phi:M\xrightarrow\sim L$, $a\mapsto(\theta_r(a))_r$. Its value on $e_i$ is $(\mathrm d(t_i\bmod\mathfrak n^r))_r=\widehat{\mathrm d}(t_i)$, proving the basis assertion.

source.place: Tag 0317 (definition-complete), and Tag 032C (remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary), via the cited variable-adic completeness statement; finite coordinatewise lifting written out.

proof.text: For $h\in D$, [lem-trf-power-series-adic-gradient-control] gives $\mathrm d(h\bmod\mathfrak n^r)=\theta_r((\partial_i h)_i)$ at every positive level. Equality of compatible families now gives $\widehat{\mathrm d}(h)=\Phi((\partial_i h)_i)=\sum_i(\partial_i h)\widehat{\mathrm d}(t_i)$, as asserted.

proof_origin.place: Explicit finite-truncation and shifted-lift inverse-limit proof using Tags 00RU (lemma-differential-seq), 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring), 02HQ (lemma-differential-mod-power-ideal), and 032C (remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary). These tags supply the finite-level ingredients and the completeness context; the continuous inverse-limit statement is the auxiliary argument written here, not a claim that Curves Tag 0C4D states it.

lean.statement: theorem formalPowerSeriesContinuousDifferentials_free (F : Type u) [Field F] (n : ℕ) : ∃ b : Module.Basis (Fin n) (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F) (KaehlerDifferential.Continuous F (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F) (Ideal.span (Set.range (MvPowerSeries.X : Fin n → MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F)))), (∀ i : Fin n, b i = KaehlerDifferential.continuousD F (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F) (Ideal.span (Set.range (MvPowerSeries.X : Fin n → MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F))) (MvPowerSeries.X i)) ∧ ∀ h : MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F, KaehlerDifferential.continuousD F (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F) (Ideal.span (Set.range (MvPowerSeries.X : Fin n → MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F))) h = ∑ i : Fin n, (MvPowerSeries.pderiv F i h) • b i
lean.note: Uses the landed compatible-family module and canonical derivation of def-trf-continuous-kahler-differentials. Existence of the specified Module.Basis expresses both freeness and the equivalent coordinate-map isomorphism. No object is replaced by its proposed free model.
